transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

I can't diagnose that problem with your fridge freezer here yet, so I won't guess at a cause or a part. If there's any burning smell, sparking, smoke or water near the electrics, stop using it and switch it off at the wall. Otherwise an appliance engineer can look at it, or tell me about a different problem with it.
Well, it's a sort of hot plastic, electrical burning smell, mostly round the back of the fridge. The plug feels a bit warm too, and I sometimes hear a buzzing from the back. Should I switch it off?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell (or signs of overheating) can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using the appliance now, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't use it again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer.
